articles.title: 'False': In rare move, Pak army reacts after rumours swirl of Imran Khan's death
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistan’s military has denied reports suggesting jailed former prime minister Imran Khan has died, journalist Wajahat Khan clarified in a video messa.
articles.body: Pakistan’s military has denied reports suggesting jailed former prime minister Imran Khan has died, journalist Wajahat Khan clarified in a video message."For the first time In several months, the ISPR has broken its silence. It has called my reporting fake. I am glad that the ISPR has responded. Fake or whatever, because that means Imran is alive. We have forced them to respond after months of deafening, chilling, frustrating silence," Pakistani journalist Wajahat Khan clarified in a video.The controversy began after journalist Khan claimed that three senior officers at Pakistan’s General Headquarters (GHQ) had expressed fears that Imran Khan may no longer be alive. However, he had stressed that the information was not independently verified and described it as apprehension rather than confirmed news.Speaking of his sources, who had told him about Imran Khan's news, he said, "Let's be very clear. They did not confirm that Imran Khan is dead. Let me repeat. They did not confirm that Imran Khan is dead. Let's be unequivocally clear about that. What they confirmed is their own profound, paralyzing fear that the worst may have happened or is likely to happen, may have happened or is likely to happen. Why? Because the military currently is uncharacteristically, terrifyingly, and chillingly silent and tight-lipped."The remarks came amid growing concerns over the 73-year-old former prime minister's health, with his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party demanding that his family members and personal doctors be allowed to meet him.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: '30 civilans killed': Baloch activist shares video of 'Pakistani war crime', seeks US intervention
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Mir Yar Baloch, a Baloch leader, has accused Pakistan's military of carrying out an airstrike in Balochistan that allegedly killed 30 civilians, inclu.
articles.body: Mir Yar Baloch, a Baloch leader, has accused Pakistan's military of carrying out an airstrike in Balochistan that allegedly killed 30 civilians, including women, children and infants.He claimed that video footage from the August 12 attack in Surab's Gidar Goandhan area provides evidence of the military operation and said he plans to take the matter to the International Criminal Court."The Republic of Balochistan has obtained video footage of the Surab Air Strike conducted by the external terrorist forces of Pakistan on 12th August, which killed 30 innocent Balochistan civilians including women, children, and infants and injured dozens more. The missile debris clearly visible in the video constitute irrefutable proof of Pakistan's terrorism. They also thoroughly expose Pakistan's military spokesperson, DG ISPR, who deliberately misled the global community on national media by claiming the attack was merely an IED blast on the ground," Mir Yar Baloch wrote on X.Baloch leader seeks US sanctionsMir Yar Baloch has urged the US administration to impose sanctions on Pakistan and halt military support, including F-16 engine spare parts and upgrades to fighter jets and missile programmes."The Republic of Balochistan urges the Trump administration to impose strict economic sanctions on Pakistan, cancel the delivery of spare parts for F-16 engines, and halt all upgradation package to its fighter jets and missile program. The Pakistan military and air force are massively employing these very weapons and aircraft against the people of the independent Republic of Balochistan. Washington must hold Pakistan fully accountable for its war crimes in Balochistan," he added.ALSO READ | Peace talks abroad, protests at home: The many contradictions shaping Pakistan todayThe two sides have given sharply different accounts of what happened in Surab, leaving the circumstances of the incident and the actual civilian death toll disputed.Pakistan disputes airstrike allegationsPakistan's military has rejected the claim of an airstrike and said the casualties were caused by a premature explosion involving a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device allegedly being assembled by militants.The Inter-Services Public Relations said the initial blast killed eight militants and that a secondary explosion involving other explosives stored at the site also caused civilian deaths."However, the blast and secondary detonation of other explosives stored there by the terrorists of Indian Proxy have also reportedly caused tragic casualties of three nearby civilians," the ISPR said.The military said Pakistani forces and Balochistan Police subsequently killed 10 more individuals, taking the reported militant death toll to 18. Two Pakistani soldiers were also injured during the exchange of fire.Protests erupt over reported civilian deathsThe competing accounts have come amid protests in Balochistan following reports of civilian deaths in the Surab area.The Balochistan Post reported that more than 20 people were initially killed and at least 16 injured in the incident. Some local residents, however, claimed that the actual death toll could be higher.ALSO READ | Pakistani minister in Balochistan province escapes armed attack on convoyCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 10 dead as torrential rain lashes southwest China; over 21,000 evacuated
articles.summary: China News: Ten people died in two disasters in southwest China amid torrential rain. Five people died after accumulated rainwater caused a roof and wall to colla.
articles.body: Ten people died in two disasters in southwest China amid torrential rain. Five people died after accumulated rainwater caused a roof and wall to collapse in Sichuan province. Five others died in a landslide at a construction site in Guangxi region.Disaster prevention authorities evacuated 21,784 people as a precaution after heavy downpours hit several areas, including Chengdu and Zigong.The Sichuan collapse occurred on Tuesday at a home in Changning county, where people had gathered for a dinner party to celebrate children's college entrance results. China Central Television (CCTV), China's state broadcaster, reported the deaths on Wednesday.Three people died at the house, while two others died in hospital, where 17 injured people were receiving treatment. It was unclear whether children or young people were among those included in the casualty figures, news agency Reuters reported.Sichuan authorities also issued a heavy-rain alert this week and warned of disaster risks. CCTV said two incidents caused by torrential rain since Tuesday had cut road access in mountainous Garze and Aba.In Guangxi, a landslide buried five people at a construction site on Monday. Rescue workers later recovered all five dead, according to CCTV.Heavy rain has affected Guangxi since summer began, as it has many other parts of southwest China. Officials had earlier identified loose sand and gravel in the high mountain canyon area as a potential landslide risk.Authorities are investigating what caused Monday's landslide in Guangxi.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump-Bibi tensions deepen? US officials frustrated by Israel’s Syria strikes: Report
articles.summary: Israel’s latest airstrikes on a Syrian airbase have frustrated senior US officials and exposed fresh tensions between US President Donald Trump and
articles.body: Israel’s latest airstrikes on a Syrian airbase have frustrated senior US officials and exposed fresh tensions between US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Axios reported, citing US and Israeli officials.The strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase in north-western Syria came as the Trump administration has sought to strengthen ties with Syria’s government under President Ahmed al-Sharaa and views its engagement with Damascus as a foreign policy achievement. Trump also maintains close ties with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, whose government strongly backs the new Syrian leadership.At least eight Israeli bombs struck the runways and several hangars at the airbase early Tuesday, about 45 miles from the Turkish border. Israel told the White House the operation was intended to deter Turkey from sending sophisticated weapons systems to the facility and prevent a broader military buildup there, according to Axios. The strike caused damage but no casualties.Israel’s Prime Minister’s Office said Damascus had been close to violating an agreed security status quo by allowing Turkish troops to deploy at the base."The Prime Minister's Office: Israel and Syria agreed to a status quo in security matters, which Syria was on the verge of breaching by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo. Israel repeatedly warned Syria that such a deployment would pose a threat to Israel's security. Syria chose to ignore these warnings," it said."Israel will not tolerate threats to its security, and would welcome a return to the status quo," it added.Turkey rejected Israel’s justification. "There was no Turkish presence at the airbase. Israel is inventing pretexts to bomb neighboring countries and destabilize the region," a Turkish official said.The US response, however, was unusually critical. Tom Barrack, Trump’s special presidential envoy for Syria and Iraq, said the strikes were an "unnecessary escalation" and did not advance regional stability. "We are deeply concerned that the confirmed Israeli airstrikes on Abu al-Duhur Airbase constitute an unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability," Barrack said.Axios reported that some senior US officials believe Netanyahu’s decision may have also been influenced by Israel’s October election. US officials said Syria had not taken hostile steps against Israel and had spent months seeking a security arrangement to reduce tensions.According to one US official, Damascus had pushed for weeks for a joint coordination centre in Jordan involving the US and Israel to manage incidents and prevent escalation. Israel, however, refused to operationalise the centre and instead increased military incursions into southern Syria, the official said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Microsoft is hiring a legal engineer to teach lawyers across the company how to…
articles.summary: Tech News News: Microsoft has spent the past two years telling everyone else that AI is about to change how work gets done. Now it wants someone to prove the point in.
articles.body: Microsoft has spent the past two years telling everyone else that AI is about to change how work gets done. Now it wants someone to prove the point inside its own legal department. The company has posted a job for a principal legal engineer, an unusual hybrid role that asks for a practising attorney who can also ship software, with base pay topping out at $278,900 a year.The listing, spotted on LinkedIn this week by Business Insider, puts the hire inside Microsoft's Customer & Partner Solutions group, the arm that supports the company's commercial business. The work is deliberately hands-on: building AI agents, sharpening prompts, and training attorneys and paralegals to actually use the tools. "This is a role for a builder," Microsoft wrote in the job description, adding that the person will partner directly with engineering rather than advise from the sidelines. Microsoft did not respond to Business Insider's request for comment.Why Microsoft wants a lawyer who can also write softwareLawyers were the corporate world's great tech holdouts for decades, understandably nervous about tools that could get one detail wrong in a 90-page agreement. That resistance is thinning. Clients are now pushing outside firms toward tools like Harvey and Claude for Legal to turn work around faster and bill less for it.The same pressure has moved in-house. Legal teams are betting that software can handle contract edits and policy drafting, letting them keep more of the early work and hand outside counsel matters that are already halfway done. Microsoft has a head start here because it builds some of these tools itself. Its lawyers already use Copilot for routine work, including contract review, where it compares a draft against similar agreements, flags issues and suggests edits that match company policy. Harvey is being rolled out across Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs.The legal engineer job is spreading from startups to Big TechUntil recently, legal engineer was mostly a startup title, filled by ex-lawyers with technical chops who sat close to customers. Palantir posted its own embedded legal engineer role last month, promising to turn manual workflows into automated ones.Microsoft wants a law degree and at least seven years of practice. Experience with Harvey or Copilot is preferred. Base pay starts at $147,000.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Toasting Sugar Adds Caramel Flavor to Your Bakes. Here’s How to Do It
articles.summary: A viral Threads post introduced a new ingredient to some: toasted sugar, or granulated caramel, popularized by food writer and author Stella Parks in 2016.
articles.body: According to one family, toasted sugar is the best thing since sliced bread. On Nov. 10, author Christopher Hawkins shared a photo on Threads of the ingredient his wife, Kris Hawkins, was preparing at their home in the West Chicago suburbs. “My wife is toasting sugar for future baking, and the whole house smells like delicious caramel,” he wrote. “Let the holidays begin!” Christopher’s photo shows a pan filled with caramel-colored, granulated sugar, something many commenters didn’t even know existed. “please have your wife come here and explain,” wrote one, and another added, “Okay hold the damn phone. I am a French pastry chef and I’ve NEVER heard of this. Absolutely genius.” Others were familiar with the concept and stepped in to enlighten. “It lightly caramelizes the sugar without melting it, which adds depth of flavor. Stella Parks is the queen of baking science, and she swears by it,” one person commented. Pastry chef and food writer Stella Parks discovered the ingredient by happy accident after finding a forgotten pan of sugar in a preheating oven. After tinkering with the process, Parks published instructions in her first book, “BraveTart: Iconic American Desserts,” which won a James Beard Foundation Award in 2018. She published the recipe on Serious Eats in 2016. Some commenters suggested making toasted sugar when blind-baking pie crust, then using it in later recipes. “So brown butter toasted sugar chocolate chip cookies is going to be my next recipe to try. Thank you very much,” another wrote. Christopher’s post garnered over 1.1 million views. “Sometimes you post things on Instagram, and you get a lot of contrary opinions,” Christopher tells TODAY.com. “Everyone was so positive about it.” Kris says she’s been toasting sugar for 8 or 9 years and uses it in everything from cookies to agua de jamaica. She typically makes a 20-pound batch. “Even if you make even just a basic chocolate chip cookie, it tastes richer if you have the caramel sugar in it,” she tells TODAY.com. “Until you actually try it and use it, you probably won’t have a full appreciation of it,” Kris adds. “When you start smelling it, that might, but actually using it will really make you a believer.” How Do You Make Toasted Sugar? How do you make toasted sugar without it melting? The answer is: very slowly. You might be familiar with making perfect or pure caramel, which involves melting sugar at the right temperature for the right amount of time, then adding water, butter or heavy cream to halt the process. If you heat granulated white sugar for a long time in a low-temperature oven, it doesn’t melt; instead, every granule turns into a grain of caramel. A community note on the Thread refers to a King Arthur recipe that instructs you to heat the sugar at 325 F, which I found to be too hot. (Don’t ask me or my pan full of soft caramel how I know this.) Per Parks’ instructions, heat 4 pounds of cane or beet sugar in a 9- by 13-inch baking dish at 300 F. Stir thoroughly — and she means thoroughly — every 30 minutes to break up clumps and release water vapor. If your oven runs hot, stir even more frequently. Bake to your desired color, which will take anywhere from 1 to 4 hours. (Kris says she usually bakes it for 6 to 7 hours, though.) After the sugar cools completely, store in an airtight container. Granulated caramel will keep indefinitely if kept dry, just like granulated sugar.

articles.title: EUA e Rússia se opõem a negociações sobre limitação de armas autônomas | G1
articles.standfirst: Encontro organizado pela ONU debate possível acordo para proibições e regulamentações desse tipo de arma assistida por IA. Guterres pediu ação contra 'armas impiedosas'.
articles.summary: Encontro organizado pela ONU debate possível acordo para proibições e regulamentações desse tipo de arma assistida por IA. Guterres pediu ação contra 'armas impiedosas'.
articles.body:
Uma reunião organizada pela ONU começa nesta segunda-feira (16), na Suíça, para debater uma possível limitação ao desenvolvimento e uso de armas autônomas , mas os Estados Unidos e a Rússia se opõem às negociações.

O encontro visa decidir a necessidade ou não de um acordo juridicamente vinculativo sobre proibições e regulamentações para Sistemas de Armas Autônomas Letais (LAWS, na sigla em inglês) . Os dois países, assim como outros como Israel - grandes produtores de armas -, afirmam que o direito humanitário existente já é suficiente.

➡️ A Convenção sobre Certas Armas Convencionais, tratado internacional de Direito Internacional Humanitário, assinado por 128 países em 1980, funciona como um marco geral ao qual estão vinculados diversos protocolos específicos que proíbem ou restringem categorias particulares de armamentos.

O avanço da inteligência artificial impulsionou o desenvolvimento de drones, robôs, tanques, submarinos e outros equipamentos militares capazes de matar sem intervenção humana . Armas semiautônomas, assistidas por IA, já foram utilizadas na Ucrânia, no Sudão e no Oriente Médio, apesar das preocupações éticas.

Antonio Guterres discursa na 81ª Assembleia Geral da ONU, em Nova York — Foto: Shannon Stapleton/Reuters

Na abertura das negociações em Genebra, o secretário-geral das Nações Unidas, Antônio Guterres, se pronunciou através de uma mensagem em vídeo e pediu que os países ajam contra essas "armas impiedosas".

"A natureza da guerra está mudando. Novas tecnologias apresentam novos desafios humanitários, legais, éticos e de segurança. Apelo a vocês para que avancem rumo à negociação de um instrumento juridicamente vinculativo para regulamentar os sistemas de armas autônomas — incluindo proibições e restrições claras", disse Guterres, instando os países "a aproveitarem este momento. Tomem medidas para impedir o uso e a disseminação dessas armas impiedosas".

Os EUA preferem diretrizes a regras vinculativas sobre sistemas de armas autônomas letais (LAWS, na sigla em inglês), argumentando que o direito internacional já fornece uma estrutura para reger a guerra. Propuseram um mandato de cinco anos para negociações visando um acordo não vinculativo.

A Rússia não declarou publicamente sua posição para as negociações, mas já resistiu anteriormente a propostas de um acordo juridicamente vinculativo. Segundo um diplomata ocidental de alto escalão, o país planeja impedir que a União Europeia, observadora nas negociações, tenha a palavra.

O Comitê Internacional da Cruz Vermelha, juntamente com o papa, alerta para os perigos das armas autônomas e para a regulamentação do apoio a elas, e afirma que o direito humanitário não aborda suficientemente os riscos específicos das armas autônomas.

articles.summary: Evento será realizado em 19 de novembro, em Quixeramobim, e deve reunir até 400 participantes para discutir os caminhos para o empreendedorismo feminino
articles.body:
As inscrições já estão disponíveis — Foto: divulgação

O Delas Day 2026 – edição Sertão Central será realizado no próximo dia 19 de novembro, em Quixeramobim, reunindo cerca de 400 mulheres empreendedoras, produtoras rurais, artesãs e lideranças femininas da região. A iniciativa é promovida pelo Sebrae Ceará e integra as ações de apoio ao desenvolvimento de negócios liderados por mulheres no Ceará.

Realizado no Dia Mundial do Empreendedorismo Feminino, o evento terá como foco a discussão de oportunidades de mercado, acesso a crédito, qualificação e desenvolvimento empresarial. A proposta é reunir mulheres que já empreendem e aquelas que desejam iniciar uma atividade própria, criando um ambiente de troca de experiências e aproximação com instituições que oferecem suporte ao desenvolvimento dos pequenos negócios.

A atuação do Sebrae nesse segmento envolve iniciativas que acompanham diferentes etapas da trajetória empreendedora, desde a identificação de oportunidades e a estruturação de uma ideia até a gestão, a inovação e a ampliação dos negócios. Por meio de capacitações, consultorias, orientação empresarial e programas como o Sebrae Delas, a instituição trabalha questões relacionadas à gestão, ao planejamento, ao acesso a mercados e ao desenvolvimento de competências necessárias à administração de uma empresa.

No Sertão Central, o encontro também abre espaço para dar visibilidade aos negócios conduzidos por mulheres e às atividades econômicas desenvolvidas nos municípios da região. A participação de instituições financeiras e entidades do Sistema S amplia o contato das empreendedoras com serviços de orientação, qualificação e alternativas de financiamento.

articles.title: Papa Leão XIV encerra viagem de 12 dias pela América do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: Pontífice passou duas décadas no país como missionário e bispo. Visita terminou nesta segunda-feira (16), com missa em Lima.
articles.summary: Leão XIV encerrou visita ao Peru nesta segunda-feira (16). Pontífice passou duas décadas no país como padre missionário e bispo.
articles.body:
O papa Leão XIV deixa encontro com fiéis e representantes de manifestações de religiosidade popular no Parque Arqueológico Nacional de Saqsaywaman, em Cusco, no Peru, no décimo dia de sua viagem apostólica de 12 dias pela América do Sul. — Foto: Andrew Medichini / AP Photo/Andrew Medichini

O papa Leão XIV se despediu nesta segunda-feira (16) do Peru , país onde viveu por duas décadas como padre missionário e bispo. O pontífice encerrou uma viagem de 12 dias pela América do Sul, que incluiu visitas ao Uruguai, à Argentina e ao Peru.

Ao deixar a residência do Vaticano em Lima, Leão XIV agradeceu aos peruanos por acompanhá-lo durante a visita.

Em seguida, disse, em espanhol, “até mais”.

O último dia da viagem começou com uma visita a um lar de idosos na região de Callao. O local foi acompanhado pelo então padre Robert Prevost durante a pandemia de Covid-19. Depois, o papa celebrou uma missa em uma base aérea da capital peruana. A expectativa era de que até 1 milhão de pessoas participassem da cerimônia.

Viagem foi marcada por reencontro com o Peru

Nascido em Chicago, nos Estados Unidos, Leão XIV passou cerca de 20 anos no Peru como missionário e bispo . O país é considerado por ele sua segunda pátria. O pontífice também tem cidadania peruana.

Durante a chegada ao país, ele afirmou que o Peru era sua “patria”, palavra em espanhol que significa pátria, e cantou o hino nacional ao lado da presidente Keiko Fujimori.

Ao longo da viagem, o papa percorreu diferentes regiões do país, incluindo áreas dos Andes e da floresta amazônica. No domingo (15), último dia completo da visita, ele passou por Chiclayo, cidade onde atuou como bispo, Cusco, nos Andes, e Pucallpa, na Amazônia, antes de retornar a Lima.

O deslocamento foi marcado por mudanças bruscas de clima e altitude. Em Cusco, por exemplo, o pontífice esteve a cerca de 3.400 metros acima do nível do mar, em uma região de temperaturas mais baixas e menor concentração de oxigênio.

A atuação de Leão XIV no Peru e à frente da Igreja Católica tem sido comparada à trajetória de São Toríbio de Mogrovejo, primeiro arcebispo de Lima.

Toríbio viveu entre 1538 e 1606 e é lembrado por denunciar abusos cometidos por colonizadores espanhóis contra indígenas e pessoas escravizadas. Ele também percorreu a pé e a cavalo o território de sua arquidiocese para atender fiéis.

O religioso aprendeu quéchua e aimará para se comunicar com comunidades indígenas e supervisionou a tradução de ensinamentos da Igreja para essas línguas.

A viagem de Leão XIV pela América do Sul começou em 6 de novembro, no Uruguai, e passou pela Argentina, país de origem de seu antecessor, o papa Francisco . Francisco não chegou a visitar a Argentina durante seu pontificado.

A realização da viagem chegou a ser colocada em dúvida depois que Leão XIV passou por uma cirurgia relacionada a um câncer no pulmão, em 13 de outubro, em Roma. No início da visita, porém, o pontífice afirmou que não tinha dúvidas de que conseguiria cumprir a agenda .

articles.title: Mãe acusada de matar filhos nos EUA terá novo julgamento em 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Júri não chegou a um veredicto no primeiro julgamento. Promotoria pretende manter as três acusações de homicídio em primeiro grau.
articles.summary: Lindsay Clancy será julgada novamente a partir de março de 2027. Primeiro julgamento terminou sem veredicto após impasse entre jurados.
articles.body:
Ao lado de seu advogado, Lindsay Clancy, acusada de homicídio por matar os três filhos, olha ao júri durante julgamento de seu caso, em 1º de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Greg Derr/ Pool via Reuters

A americana Lindsay Clancy , acusada de matar os três filhos, passará por um novo julgamento a partir de 29 de março de 2027 . A data foi marcada menos de um ano depois de o primeiro julgamento terminar sem um veredito, porque os jurados não chegaram a um consenso.

A promotoria informou à Justiça que pretende manter as três acusações de homicídio em primeiro grau contra Clancy .

A defesa sustenta que Clancy não deve ser responsabilizada criminalmente pelas mortes já que a mulher sofria de psicose pós-parto e teve um surto no momento do crime.

Se for condenada por homicídio em primeiro grau, ela poderá receber prisão perpétua sem direito à liberdade condicional .

Caso seja considerada inocente por falta de responsabilidade criminal, poderá ser internada em um hospital psiquiátrico estadua l, com avaliações periódicas determinadas pela Justiça.

➡️ No primeiro julgamento, o júri ficou dividido após um dos jurados não concordar com a possibilidade de inocentar Clancy . O juiz então declarou o julgamento encerrado, sem um veredicto. Leia mais abaixo.

O caso de Lindsay Clancy envolve a morte dos três filhos pequenos da americana, em janeiro de 2023, em uma residência na cidade de Duxbury, no estado de Massachusetts. As crianças foram encontradas inconscientes e levadas a hospitais, mas não sobreviveram.

As vítimas eram Cora, de 5 anos, Dawson, de 3, e Callan, de 8 meses. Segundo a investigação, as crianças foram estranguladas com faixas elásticas de exercício no porão da casa da família. O pai, Patrick Clancy, encontrou os filhos ao voltar de um compromisso. Os dois mais velhos morreram no mesmo dia. O bebê morreu três dias depois, em um hospital.

Depois do crime, Lindsay tentou tirar a própria vida ao pular de uma janela do segundo andar. Ela sofreu ferimentos graves e ficou paralisada da cintura para baixo. Na época, trabalhava como enfermeira em uma maternidade e tinha passado por tratamento psiquiátrico nas semanas anteriores.

A defesa afirma que Clancy sofria de psicose pós-parto e não tinha consciência do que fazia. Os advogados dizem que ela teve um episódio psicótico e ouviu vozes que a mandavam matar os filhos e a si mesma. A promotoria, por outro lado, sustenta que ela planejou os assassinatos e sabia que suas ações eram erradas.

O primeiro julgamento começou em julho de 2026 e durou quase seis semanas. Em 4 de setembro, o juiz declarou o processo encerrado sem veredicto , depois que os jurados não conseguiram chegar a um consenso. A nova sessão está marcada para 29 de março de 2027.

articles.title: Por que alguns crânios de sapos parecem até armaduras?  | G1
articles.standfirst: Característica está associada a diferentes estratégias de alimentação e defesa; estudo analisou crânios de 158 espécies de anuros.
articles.summary: Característica está associada a diferentes estratégias de alimentação e defesa; estudo analisou crânios de 158 espécies de anuros.
articles.body:
Algumas espécies de sapos, rãs e pererecas possuem crânios que lembram verdadeiras armaduras . Com relevos, protuberâncias e estruturas ósseas que ampliam a proteção da cabeça, esses animais apresentam uma característica conhecida como hiperossificação .

Em determinados casos, o esqueleto chega a formar uma espécie de capacete, com expansões que modificam completamente o formato do crânio .

Essa característica surgiu repetidas vezes ao longo da evolução dos anuros — grupo que reúne sapos, rãs e pererecas — e pode estar relacionada a diferentes estratégias de sobrevivência.

Pesquisadores da Universidade da Flórida, nos Estados Unidos, investigaram o fenômeno em um estudo publicado em 2020 na revista científica Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS).

Por que alguns crânios de sapos parecem até armaduras? Entenda o fenômeno da hiperossificação — Foto: Willianilson Pessoa

A equipe analisou imagens tridimensionais dos crânios de 158 espécies de anuros, representantes das 54 famílias reconhecidas na pesquisa, para entender como a hiperossificação surgiu e quais fatores podem estar relacionados às transformações ósseas.

Os resultados indicaram que a característica evoluiu de maneira independente cerca de 30 vezes ao longo da história do grupo.

Isso significa que diferentes linhagens desenvolveram essas modificações cranianas em momentos distintos da evolução, sem herdá-las de um único ancestral hiperossificado.

esses animais apresentam uma característica conhecida como hiperossificação — Foto: Willianilson Pessoa

A hiperossificação ocorre quando há um aumento da deposição de tecido ósseo em determinadas regiões do esqueleto . Nos anuros, o processo pode provocar alterações na superfície e no formato dos ossos do crânio.

Em manifestações mais discretas, surgem relevos, cristas e pequenas depressões na superfície óssea, formando diferentes padrões.

Em casos extremos, o crescimento ósseo pode produzir protuberâncias semelhantes a armaduras e capacetes, além de promover a união entre estruturas do esqueleto e da pele.

Essas modificações alteram o formato da cabeça e podem resultar em crânios bastante diferentes dos encontrados na maioria dos sapos, rãs e pererecas.

O estudo identificou a hiperossificação em espécies de diferentes tamanhos, desde anuros muito pequenos até animais de porte consideravelmente maior. Os resultados indicaram que o tamanho corporal não determina a presença dessa característica.

Por que desenvolver um crânio mais robusto?

Hiperossificação em crânios de anuros é tema de pesquisas — Foto: Willianilson Pessoa

Uma das principais questões investigadas pelos cientistas foi entender quais fatores ambientais e comportamentais poderiam favorecer o desenvolvimento da hiperossificação.

Os pesquisadores consideraram três possibilidades: alimentação, redução da perda de água e defesa contra predadores.

Em relação à alimentação, a pesquisa associou a hiperossificação a espécies de anuros que consomem outros vertebrados.

Nesses animais, os cientistas identificaram estruturas ósseas mais desenvolvidas e reforçadas, capazes de oferecer sustentação durante a captura e o consumo de presas maiores e mais resistentes.

Um exemplo são as espécies do gênero Ceratophrys .

Espécie Ceratophrys joazeirensis — Foto: Willianilson Pessoa

"As espécies de Ceratophrys, conhecidas como sapo-boi ou sapo-de-chifres, são predadores ativos, chamados em inglês de “Pac-Man” por consumirem quase o volume do próprio corpo, conseguindo engolir ratos que têm até 60% do seu tamanho em uma única bocada", explica o herpetólogo — especialista em afíbios e répteis — Willianilson Pessoa.

Algumas espécies também apresentam projeções semelhantes a dentes na mandíbula, chamadas de presas odontoides. Essas estruturas podem produzir ferimentos semelhantes aos de uma mordida.

Dos 11 anuros analisados que apresentavam essas projeções, nove também tinham hiperossificação e eram predadores de vertebrados.

Outra associação identificada pelos cientistas envolve uma estratégia de defesa conhecida como comportamento fragmótico.

Nesse comportamento, o animal utiliza a própria cabeça para bloquear a entrada de um abrigo, como uma cavidade em uma árvore, uma bromélia ou uma fenda entre rochas.

Assim, o crânio funciona como uma espécie de tampa, dificultando ou impedindo a entrada de predadores.

Na Caatinga, um exemplo é a perereca-de-capacete ( Corythomantis greeningi ).

Espécie Corythomantis greeningi — Foto: Willianilson Pessoa

"É um bicho mais comum na Caatinga que possui a adaptação de entrar em buracos de troncos de árvores, no chão ou em rochas e tampar o buraco com a cabeça como proteção", conta o especialista.

Alguns anuros desenvolveram cabeças largas e achatadas, com estruturas ósseas que ampliam a superfície de bloqueio.

Em determinadas espécies, a cobertura do crânio também forma pequenas aberturas próximas aos olhos, permitindo que eles sejam recolhidos para regiões protegidas pela estrutura óssea.

Os pesquisadores identificaram essa associação em diferentes linhagens de anuros, principalmente nas pererecas-de-capacete.

Outro aspecto é a presença de glândulas com um sistema de liberação de veneno associado às espinhas ósseas do crânio.

"Pererecas do grupo antes chamado de Aparasphenodon são descritas como peçonhentas por possuírem microfissuras e protuberâncias no crânio que secretam peçonha quando o animal tenta morder ou quando é manipulado com a mão, tratando-se de uma inoculação ativa e não passiva pelo toque", explica o herpetólogo, chamando a atenção para a maneira como a substância é liberada.

O especialista também destaca a presença de uma boca em formato de disco , associada ao desenvolvimento acentuado do crânio.

Boca em forma de disco da espécie Boana albomarginata — Foto: Willianilson Pessoa

“As pererecas e alguns sapos de chão predadores — até de vertebrados —, têm um desenvolvimento acentuado da boca e do crânio. Se você reparar, todas as pererecas têm essa boca em forma de disco e o crânio bem desenvolvido, o que gera um peso muito grande até para manter o próprio equilíbrio. Num galho, por exemplo, na postura quando estão sentados, eles não conseguem ficar com a cabeça inclinada com a boca na vertical: é sempre na horizontal, mesmo que o corpo esteja na vertical”.

Já a hipótese de que a hiperossificação estaria relacionada à redução da perda de água não encontrou evidências suficientes no estudo.

Crânio interfere na postura dos anuros — Foto: Willianilson Pessoa

Para investigar a origem da hiperossificação, os pesquisadores compararam os crânios de 158 espécies e reconstruíram a história evolutiva da característica.

A análise apontou aproximadamente 30 origens independentes, indicando que as modificações surgiram em diferentes grupos de anuros, distribuídos por diversas famílias e linhagens evolutivas.

Os cientistas também observaram que as espécies hiperossificadas apresentam uma taxa de evolução do formato do crânio aproximadamente duas vezes maior do que a registrada nos anuros sem a característica.

O resultado indica que a hiperossificação está associada a mudanças mais rápidas na arquitetura craniana, favorecendo o surgimento de formatos distintos ao longo da evolução.

Ao longo de milhões de anos, diferentes linhagens desenvolveram maneiras próprias de transformar a estrutura do crânio. Essas modificações ajudam a explicar parte da diversidade de formas encontrada atualmente entre sapos, rãs e pererecas.

articles.title: Assédio moral: casos crescem 22% nas regiões de Campinas e Piracicaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Aumento nas regiões acompanha o estado de São Paulo, que registrou alta de 46,9%. Ministério Público do Trabalho orienta trabalhadores a reunir provas e formalizar queixas.
articles.summary: Aumento nas regiões acompanha o estado de São Paulo, que registrou alta de 46,9%. Ministério Público do Trabalho orienta trabalhadores a reunir provas e formalizar queixas.
articles.body:
O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) registrou 753 denúncias de assédio moral feitas por trabalhadores nas regiões de Campinas (SP) e Piracicaba (SP) entre janeiro e outubro de 2026. O número representa um aumento de 22% em comparação com o mesmo período de 2025 , quando foram contabilizadas 617 queixas .

O número fez com que as regiões, juntas, alcançassem uma média de dois casos por dia . Além disso, o crescimento acompanhou a tendência no estado de São Paulo , que saltou de 4.815 para 7.077 ocorrências — alta de 46,9%.

Segundo a procuradora do Trabalho Danielle Oliveres Corrêa, o assédio moral no ambiente profissional se manifesta por meio de palavras, mensagens ou gestos que exponham o funcionário a situações humilhantes.

Kamila Brauna fez denúncia de assédio moral após ser demitida de escola em Monte Mor (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

"O assédio moral tem duas formas. O interpessoal é aquele que acontece entre pessoas que estão ou no mesmo nível hierárquico, um indivíduo em relação a outro indivíduo, um indivíduo em relação a um grupo, um grupo em relação a um indivíduo. E o assédio organizacional, diferentemente, é voltado para toda a coletividade de trabalhadores daquela empresa", explicou.

Danielle lembrou a necessidade das vítimas reunir documentos que comprovem a prática abusiva e ainda destacou a importância das denúncias para que os casos sejam investigados .

"Para que haja uma investigação e para que essa investigação chegue a uma finalização a contento, para que a gente possa propor um Termo de Ajuste de Conduta para aquela empresa, a gente precisa comprovar esse fato", disse.

"É importante que o trabalhador, mesmo que faça de forma anônima, mas que indique as provas que ele tem, se ele tiver um print de WhatsApp, por exemplo, se aquela conduta foi por escrito, um e-mail", completou.

Denilton Ricarte, que também foi demitido de escola em Monte Mor (SP), fez denúncia junto à Kamila Brauna — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Um caso que exemplifica o assédio moral ocorreu em Monte Mor (SP). A auxiliar veterinária e ex-inspetora Kamila Brauna contou ter sofrido perseguição da diretora de uma escola municipal após denunciar uma cuidadora por maus-tratos a um aluno.

"Ela começou a me perseguir. Se eu fosse para o banheiro e demorasse muito, ela ia atrás. Ela jogava piadinhas, chamava a minha atenção na frente de todo mundo. Estava todo dia tendo pico de pressão, passando mal, taquicardia. Minha ansiedade teve uma piora muito significativa, teve aumento das minhas medicações", relatou.

Kamila teve o apoio do cozinheiro Denilton Ricarte Marques da Silva, que denunciou os maus-tratos. Porém, ele também perdeu o emprego uma semana depois da colega ter sido demitida.

"A minha supervisora chegou e falou para mim: 'Denilton, olha, infelizmente repercutiu muito o que você fez, nós vamos ter de te desligar da empresa'. Aí eu falei: 'mas por quê?' Ela falou: por causa disso, você não deveria ter denunciado. Dentro de casa, nossas contas atrasaram tudo porque eles me mandaram embora no tempo de pagar o dinheiro", contou.

As vítimas levaram o caso ao MPT, que abriu investigação por assédio moral, retaliação, monitoramento invasivo e contradição.

A Prefeitura de Monte Mor informou que a Secretaria de Educação realizou uma análise administrativa e não identificou elementos suficientes para confirmar de maneira conclusiva a ocorrência de assédio moral, perseguição ou retaliação contra Kamila e Denilton.

Sobre os desligamentos, o Executivo declarou que:

Kamila: era funcionária temporária por meio de um processo seletivo e teve o vínculo encerrado por faltas injustificadas;

Denilton: era funcionário de uma empresa terceirizada, atuava como merendeiro e foi desligado pela própria prestadora do serviço.

articles.title: UFU cai duas posições, mas se mantém entre 20 melhores universidades do país; veja cursos mais bem avaliados | G1
articles.standfirst: Universidade se destaca na categoria “inovação”, ocupando o 8º lugar. Ranking avaliou 205 universidades pelo Brasil e 39 cursos.
articles.summary: Universidade se destaca na categoria “inovação”, ocupando o 8º lugar. Ranking avaliou 205 universidades pelo Brasil e 39 cursos.
articles.body:
Fachada da Universidade Federal de Uberlândia — Foto: Reprodução/TV Integração

A Universidade Federal de Uberlândia ( UFU ) está entre as vinte melhores universidades do Brasil em 2026, de acordo com dados divulgados pelo Ranking Universitário da Folha.

Em 2025, a UFU ocupava a 16ª posição e passou para a 18ª neste ano, uma queda de duas colocações. Ao todo, 205 universidades brasileiras foram avaliadas. Com isso, a universidade retorna ao lugar que ocupava em 2023. Essa é a segunda queda consecutiva no ranking, já que de 2024 para 2025 a instituição caiu do 14º para o 16º lugar.

O ranking é liderado pela Universidade de São Paulo (USP), Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) e Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG).

O levantamento considerou cinco categorias: pesquisa, ensino, mercado de trabalho, inovação e internacionalização.

A universidade se destacou em 8º lugar em inovação no Brasil e em 2º lugar em Minas Gerais. Segundo a diretora de Inovação e Transferência de Tecnologia da UFU, Luciana Carvalho, o resultado mostra uma ciência de alta qualidade e que está cada vez mais conectada com os desafios reais.

"O principal papel da inovação dentro da universidade é fazer o conhecimento produzido aqui dentro gerar impacto lá fora. A universidade pesquisa, ensina e forma pessoas, e a inovação é a ponte que leva tudo isso para a vida das pessoas, seja em um novo produto, um tratamento, uma tecnologia para o campo ou uma empresa que nasce de uma pesquisa. Inovar também é uma forma de valorizar o pesquisador: é mostrar que o trabalho dele, muitas vezes de anos, pode mudar realidades", disse.

Ainda segundo Luciana, a UFU tem diferentes caminhos para deixar as soluções criadas pelos pesquisadores mais práticas.

"Acompanhamos o pesquisador em todo o caminho. Pela Agência Intelecto, nosso Núcleo de Inovação Tecnológica, cuidamos da proteção da propriedade intelectual, como patentes, registros de software e marcas, e da transferência dessas tecnologias para empresas por meio de licenciamentos e parcerias. Contamos também com o CIAEM (Centro de Incubação de Atividades Empreendedoras), nossa incubadora, e com o TecnoUFU, o parque tecnológico, que apoiam o nascimento e o crescimento de empresas de base tecnológica. Temos o CIEU, o Centro de Inovação e Empreendedorismo Universitário, que é um espaço de encontro entre a universidade e o setor produtivo. Lá, estudantes, pesquisadores e empresas se aproximam, trocam experiências e constroem soluções juntos", completou.

O levantamento considera informações de universidades em funcionamento no Brasil e utiliza indicadores nacionais e internacionais. Foram avaliados 42 cursos universitários com o maior número de ingressantes no país. No caso da UFU, 39 dos atuais 93. Cada carreira pondera uma série de graduações da mesma área que têm diferentes nomenclaturas. Na UFU, por exemplo, o curso de Jornalismo foi incluído na nomenclatura "Comunicação".

articles.title: I survived a fire that killed my boyfriend - it was started by his brother
articles.summary: Cameron Logan was killed and Rebecca Williams suffered serious injuries after Blair Logan set the bed they were sleeping on alight.
articles.body:
After spending the night at a Hogmanay party, Cameron Logan and his girlfriend Bex Williams returned to his family home, in a quiet suburb of Glasgow, in the early hours of New Year's Day 2017.

The young couple fell asleep on an inflatable mattress in the living room.

Within hours, Cameron would be dead and Bex critically injured.

The couple were attacked by Cameron's older brother, who poured petrol over them and set fire to their bed.

Blair Logan was jailed after admitting murder and attempted murder.

Nearly a decade later, Bex is telling her story for the first time as part of BBC Scotland's Murder Case series .

Warning this article contains graphic images.

Bex was 24 and had recently finished university and started what she described as her "dream career" in radio.

"I loved my job. I loved radio reporting and news reading," she added.

"I had dreams of becoming a foreign correspondent at a big organisation like the BBC."

"My life completely changed in those 10 seconds," she told BBC Scotland.

"I was just a normal young woman in a new relationship.

"My main worries were what I was going to wear and if I could afford that extra glass of wine."

Instead, Bex woke up in intensive care days after the attack. She was on a ventilator and doctors were unsure if she would survive.

She was left with severe burns to her face and hands, and internal damage to her throat and lungs.

Bex had a breathing tube put into her windpipe and underwent 10 surgeries.

But it was damage to her vocal cords that ultimately forced her to give up her radio job. The damage to her voice is still apparent today.

Bex says she has decided to speak about the attack now to highlight the trauma she and her family went through - and make sure Cameron is remembered.

At the time of the attack the young couple were in the process of "building a life" and had just moved in together.

Cameron, 23, was at university and had ambitions of becoming a police detective.

Bex said: "There isn't a day that goes by that I don't think about Cameron, sometimes it is happy memories... sometimes it is not.

"I still can't really process what happened to him.

"It is horrific. When you actually think about what he would have experienced in his final moments."

The attack followed years of tension between the brothers.

The High Court in Glasgow heard that Blair Logan, then 26, had barely spoken to Cameron since their grandmother's death in 2013.

In the weeks before the fire, he had stored petrol in his bedroom and carried out internet searches relating to burn injuries.

On the morning of the fire, Cameron's mother, Catherine, was woken shortly after 07:00 by the family dog.

When she went downstairs, she saw a figure dressed in dark clothing in the living room.

Moments later, it was engulfed in flames.

Bex managed to crawl into the kitchen, where she put her head inside the freezer to protect herself from the heat.

Cameron's father and a neighbour helped rescue her, but Cameron could not be saved. The family dog, Gomez, also died in the fire.

Blair told police he was out running when the fire started, but was arrested two weeks later after he could not be found on CCTV on his supposed route.

Officers also found traces of petrol fumes on his clothes and a blue medical glove in his pocket, which he claimed he wore while running.

Initially, he admitted pouring petrol over the couple but claimed he had not intended to kill his brother - only "maim him".

In July 2017, he pleaded guilty to murder and attempted murder.

He was sentenced to life imprisonment, with a minimum term of 20 years.

The consequences of the attack extended far beyond the injuries Bex suffered that morning.

She has worked hard to get over the "pain, trauma and anger" she was left with.

She abandoned her ambitions of building a career in broadcasting and is now employed by Police Scotland, in a role that sees her working with family liaison officers and some of the officers involved in her case.

She says her job change is a fitting tribute to Cameron, who himself wanted to join the force.

"I know I can never bring Cameron back, but what happened to us has to mean something. So if I can help other people, that is something," she added.

Bex continues to rebuild her life. Her career has taken a different direction and she has found happiness with a new partner.

What has changed most, nearly 10 years on, is her perspective on what matters.

"I am still very career driven; my job is very important to me - but some things just feel less important now, like what am I going to wear.

"Can I afford that glass of wine? Well, tell you what, I'm going to have that glass of wine," she said.

articles.title: UK has lost more than it gained from Brexit, Burnham expected to say
articles.summary: The prime minister will say the "Brexit we were given has not worked" in a speech on Monday.
articles.body:
The prime minister is expected to argue the UK has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union in a speech ahead of a UK-EU summit later this week.

Speaking at the Lord Mayor's Banquet on Monday, Andy Burnham will compare the UK's Brexit deal to the "emperor's new clothes" - saying "a needlessly hard Brexit" created barriers for businesses and the promise to "take back control" was not delivered.

He is due to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility with the bloc at Friday's summit, after the substance of those deals was set by his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

The Conservatives have said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door".

Separately Burnham has said he wants to examine the "pros and cons" of different options for Britain's long-term relationship with the EU.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told the BBC the prime minister would lay out these potential options after the UK-EU summit.

However, Burnham has ruled out major changes before the next general election.

Burnham is expected to say on Monday: "It's like the emperor's new clothes – where no-one is prepared to say the obvious truth. Well, I say it as I see it. And to be frank, the emperor has nothing on.

"The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we have gained."

Ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit, Burnham will set out three tests for any agreement.

Firstly, that it must be consistent with Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledge that there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement".

He will also say it must improve the original Brexit deal and bring it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016.

Finally, he will say any deal must pass the "Makerfield test" of providing tangible improvements to people's everyday lives - a reference to voters in Burnham's Greater Manchester constituency.

He will say the prospect of a new deal is a "win-win" and illustrates a "new approach".

"Not adversarial. No longer burning bridges. But being constructive and positive - showing that we can come together to confront shared challenges."

UK will have 'voice' but no vote on EU food rules in Brexit reset

Burnham says 'win-win' deal can be agreed between UK and EU

Burnham's push for closer EU ties causes ripples in his party and others

This week's summit will see the UK seek to agree further changes to former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer's deal, struck in May 2025, covering fishing, trade and other areas.

The UK and EU have agreed a draft deal on removing post-Brexit checks from food and agriculture exports ahead of the meeting.

The government argues the agreement will help cut costs for businesses and could bring down prices for shoppers.

However, critics say the deal will make the UK a "rule taker" from Brussels, aligning with EU regulations without being able to vote on them.

Similar texts for deals on emissions trading and a youth travel and work scheme have also been circulated to EU nations.

These deals were close to being finalised under Sir Keir, with only some details still to be worked out.

New campaign against EU membership launches ahead of UK-EU summit

Brexit referendum 'possible' in Labour election manifesto, says Burnham

As a candidate in the Makerfield by-election that propelled his return to Parliament, Burnham had promised not to "re-run" Brexit arguments and said he was "not proposing that the UK considers rejoining the EU".

However, since becoming prime minister he has said he wants to explore a different long-term relationship with the bloc.

He has suggested potential options for the future could range from no changes to the UK-EU relationship, to rejoining the customs union, the single market or a fresh referendum on full EU membership.

The prime minister has stressed any changes would require a mandate from the public at a general election.

Boris Johnson, who was prime minister when the UK left the EU in 2020 and negotiated the original Brexit deal, has warned Burnham against "wasting his premiership" on Europe.

He told the Daily Telegraph he believed the public would back Brexit again if Burnham forced another vote on the issue.

"It is madness to escalate the Brexit issue as your political priority," Johnson told the paper.

"He will impale himself and his party on this point, and he needs to move off it because he won't win – because the reality is that people are not fools."

Deputy Conservative leader Alex Burghart accused Burnham of "reopening a debate the country settled long ago, while ignoring the challenges facing Britain today".

Reform UK has said one of the "key benefits" of Brexit is that Britain no longer has to "adhere to ridiculous EU rules", and argued that any form of alignment could have a negative impact on the country's trade policy.

The Liberal Democrats have said the draft deal on food exports is a "patch, not a fix" and that the "real solution is to re-join the single market and to establish a customs union with the EU".

The Green Party of England and Wales has called for the UK to re-join the customs union, with leader Zack Polanski previously saying "full membership of the EU remains the best option for the UK".

articles.title: Clyde ready for 'heavy metal football' as rock band sponsors club
articles.summary: Metalcore act Bleed From Within have also co-designed the new third kit for the Bully Wee, who now play in the band's home town of Hamilton.
articles.body:
The former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp once described the high-octane style of his teams as "heavy metal football."

Now Scottish League Two side Clyde have gone a step further than Klopp's metaphor - by agreeing a sponsorship deal with a rock band.

Metalcore act Bleed From Within have also co-designed the new third kit for the club nicknamed "the Bully Wee", who now play in the band's home town of Hamilton, South Lanarkshire.

The group, who have released seven albums, said the new partnership was "an opportunity not to be missed".

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

The band's singer Scott Kennedy said: "Working with Clyde FC was a no brainer.

"Given our shared connections to Glasgow, where we played our first shows and Hamilton, where the band was formed, we knew this made sense.

"We couldn't be happier with how the shirts turned out and we look forward to supporting the guys throughout the season and beyond."

The new shirt features colour tones from the group's 2020 record Fracture and is designed to appeal to "communities in football and music".

Clyde chief executive David Alexander said: "We are beyond excited to work with Bleed From Within on our third shirt for the 26/27 season.

"As a club who thrive on living outside the box and doing things differently, we had no hesitation when given the option to team up with an iconic name in the metal industry from Glasgow.

"A number of staff members already familiar with the artist, gave immediate excitement at the potential to turn heads and raise visibility of the club through such a great band."

Alexander added that since the project was floated the club had "enjoyed watching the band storm across the European festival circuit".

Bleed From Within worked on the shirt design with Clyde's technical partner Terrace, who said the group had shown great enthusiasm for the idea.

The band join a long line of music acts who have become involved with football clubs.

Ed Sheeran - who was also a minority owner of the club - sponsored Ipswich Town for four seasons, starting in 2021.

Last year rock band Franz Ferdinand backed youth football team Symington Tinto 2014s, with the group's logo appearing on kits .

In October US rock band Wheatus agreed to sponsor a Worcestershire youth football team.

And in the 1990s Clydebank were sponsored by the pop band Wet Wet Wet, who came from the West Dunbartonshire town.

Other acts like the Libertines, Fontaines D.C and Mogwai have also been involved in sponsorship of teams in the past.

articles.title: At least 11 killed in blaze on Thailand’s Phuket island
articles.summary: Authorities are investigating the cause of the fire, which also injured 16, but have ruled out arson.
articles.body:
A fire in ⁠a commercial ⁠building on Thailand’s southern resort island of Phuket has ⁠killed at least 11 people and injured 16 others, according to police.

The blaze in the tourist hub of Patong started at about 3:17am on Monday (20:17 GMT on Sunday) in a building housing a restaurant, rented accommodation and a motorcycle rental shop, and later spread to several other buildings nearby.

Phuket police commander Surachai Sooksai said officers are still investigating the cause of the fire, but an initial investigation found that an electrical transformer near the building had exploded shortly before the fire started, ruling out arson.

Phuket Governor Chodnarin Koedsom said the rental shop had about 100 motorcycles, along with stored gas, engine oil, plastic materials and tyres. He said these combustible materials may have contributed to the rapid spread of the fire and the thick, toxic smoke.

Of the 16 people injured, the authorities said, 15 were Thai and one was a Myanmar national, adding that no tourists were among those injured or killed.

The injured were treated at a hospital for smoke inhalation and injuries from broken glass.

Thailand’s approach to health and safety regulations, especially in bars and nightclubs has long raised concerns.

In July, a crowded bar in the capital, Bangkok, was engulfed in flames and smoke, killing about 40 people after an electrical short circuit triggered the blaze, authorities said.

Four people were killed and many more injured in a fire that swept through a club popular with tourists on Phuket in 2012.

A fire tore through a Bangkok club during New Year celebrations in 2009, killing 67 people and injuring more than 200.

articles.title: UK weather: Met Office warnings for snow as temperatures plummet
articles.summary: A spell of colder, wintry weather will grip some northern parts of the UK, bringing a threat of ice and hill snow at times.
articles.body:
A spell of cold and wintry weather is set to grip northern areas of the UK early this week, bringing the threat of ice and hill snow.

A yellow weather warning for snow comes into effect in the very early hours of Tuesday following a blast of Arctic air pushing across the UK causing temperatures to plummet.

Cold health alerts for parts of northern England also remain in force from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) until 09:00 GMT on Thursday.

Some snow is forecast over the hills and mountains in the north over the coming days but the wintry chill will be fairly short-lived in the south, where temperatures will rebound to above average by midweek.

Monday morning started on a chilly note for all parts. The coldest conditions were seen across the northern half of the UK with northern England, Scotland and Northern Ireland waking up to a sharp frost with some wintry flurries over the hills.

Tulloch Bridge in Scotland recorded an overnight low of -7.7C making it the coldest night of the season so far.

Temperatures in the south generally remained a few degrees above freezing.

Cold health alerts, issued by the UKHSA, are currently in force across north-west England, north-east England, Yorkshire and the Humber until 09:00 GMT on Thursday.

These alerts are only issued in England and are aimed at health and social care professionals.

A Met Office weather warning for ice from Sunday evening into Monday morning across northern and eastern Scotland as well as parts of Cumbria, Northumberland and Durham has now expired.

Though Monday will be dry and bright for many places, wintry showers will affect some eastern parts of England and Scotland, with these falling as sleet or snow over high ground.

Afternoon maximum temperatures will be a chilly 4-8C in most places - a few degrees below the seasonal average.

Later in the day, the next front will approach from the south-west bringing milder air and some heavy and persistent rain.

As this band of rain then moves northwards overnight into Tuesday, a further spell of hill snow may develop.

A yellow weather warning for snow is set to come into effect on Tuesday from midnight until 11:00 GMT, covering parts of the Midlands, north-east and north-west England, North Yorkshire and south-west Scotland.

Where snow does accumulate, depths of 1-5cm are likely, although some locations above 300-400m could see 5-15cm.

Some roads and railways are likely to be affected, resulting in longer travel times by road, bus and train services. Power cuts are also possible.

Further south, Tuesday will be a very different day with blustery conditions and some heavy showers.

This battleground of colder, drier conditions in the north and milder, wetter weather in the south will continue into the middle of the week.

You can keep up to date with your local forecast by checking BBC Weather online and on the app .

articles.title: Huge waves pummel the California coast, forcing closure of iconic piers
articles.summary: The California coast was pummeled again by huge waves that inundated beaches, flooded local streets and forced the closure of iconic piers.
articles.body: SAN FRANCISCO — The California coast was pummeled again Sunday by huge waves that inundated beaches, flooded local streets and forced the closure of iconic piers. The National Weather Service office for the Bay Area warned that surf up to 35 feet (10.6 meters) was possible, along with dangerous rip currents and sneaker waves. “Stay out of the water, stay off rocks and jetties, and never turn your back on the ocean!” the weather service said on social media. On Saturday, waves above 50 feet (15.2 meters) were recorded in San Mateo County, just south of San Francisco. Surfers weren’t deterred, taking advantage of giant waves at the famous Mavericks Beach near Half Moon Bay. Farther south, the Santa Cruz County Sheriff’s Office issued an evacuation warning near the coastal town of Capitola that took the brunt of the powerful surf. In Southern California, several piers, including ones in Ventura, Manhattan Beach, Huntington Beach and San Diego’s Pacific Beach, were closed during the weekend as they were slammed by waves. Several inches of water submerged the strand in Orange County’s Seal Beach and flooded beachfront homes. At La Jolla Cove near San Diego, famous for its lounging sea lions, water overflowed the beach and crashed up a staircase leading to the sand. Conditions were calming by Sunday afternoon, but large waves were expected all week, forecasters warned. The ongoing super El Niño has warmed the ocean, causing seawater to expand.

articles.title: Mexico’s Guadalajara cartel founder dies in hospital aged 80
articles.summary: Miguel Angel Felix ​Gallardo, founder of one of Mexico’s first major drug cartels whose conviction for the 1985 killing of ‌a U.S. DEA drug-enforcement agent made him one of the country’s most notorious traffickers, died in hospital on Sunday at age 80.
articles.body: MEXICO CITY/GUADALAJARA, Nov 15 — Miguel Angel Felix ​Gallardo, founder of one of Mexico’s first major drug cartels whose conviction for the 1985 killing of ‌a U.S. drug-enforcement agent made him one of the country’s most notorious traffickers, died in hospital on Sunday at age 80. Local security authorities said Felix Gallardo was transferred to a private hospital in the western city of Guadalajara two days ago but suffered multiple organ failure and ​died around 2 p.m. on Sunday. Imprisoned since 1989, Felix Gallardo was an inmate in a maximum-security prison in ​western Jalisco state, though his lawyers repeatedly sought house arrest on the grounds of his deteriorating ⁠health. Rising to prominence in the 1970s, the former cartel kingpin was an architect of Mexico’s modern drug-trafficking trade, igniting a ​series of turf wars that have led to hundreds of thousands of deaths and disappearances in ensuing decades. Born in 1946 in ​Culiacan, Sinaloa, a northwestern state that would later become synonymous with narco-trafficking, he worked as a police officer and bodyguard for a local governor then became a powerful criminal capo known as the “boss of bosses.” Felix Gallardo and others set up the cartel in Guadalajara, the Jalisco state ​capital and a fast-growing economic powerhouse, becoming the first to move cocaine to the U.S. on a massive scale and ​to forge an alliance with Colombian drug barons, including Pablo Escobar’s Medellin cartel. His narcotics empire expanded in the 1970s and 1980s thanks to ‌bribes ⁠that won protection from corrupt officials and innovations like using light aircraft to move drugs across the continent, supported by fellow kingpins like Rafael Caro Quintero. His legal battles stretched across decades. Arrested in 1989, Felix Gallardo was sentenced to 40 years in prison on drug-trafficking and weapons charges tied to the Guadalajara cartel. While already incarcerated, he faced a separate prosecution over the 1985 ​kidnapping and murder of U.S. ​Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique “Kiki” ⁠Camarena and Mexican pilot Alfredo Zavala Avelar. Camarena’s killing caused a diplomatic dispute with Washington, which pressed Mexico hard to arrest those involved. In 2017, a federal court found Felix Gallardo guilty in ​that case and imposed a further 37-year sentence. He denied responsibility for the killings. His ​rise and fall ⁠was portrayed on screen by Mexican actor Diego Luna in the 2018 hit Netflix series “Narcos: Mexico.” Felix Gallardo suffered poor health in his final years, and was blind in one eye, practically deaf and unable to walk on his own by the time Spanish-language U.S. ⁠network ​Telemundo interviewed him in prison in 2021. He maintained his innocence. NBCUniversal is the parent company of NBC News and Telemundo “Thirty-two years have ​passed... That’s an eternity for a man who did not commit any crime,” he said.

articles.title: AI cheating scandal spooks South Korea ahead of high-stakes college entrance exam
articles.summary: Days before South Korea comes to a standstill for its all-important college entrance exam, the nation is reeling after the top scorer on its tax accountant test was found to have cheated with a hidden camera and artificial intelligence.
articles.body: Days before South Korea comes to a standstill for its all-important college entrance exam, the nation is reeling after the top scorer on its tax accountant test was found to have cheated with a hidden camera and artificial intelligence. The scandal has left authorities scrambling to prevent cheating on the exam, which will be taken Thursday by more than 500,000 students, as concerns grow that AI and smart devices are making fraud harder to detect. Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin on Monday rejected calls by some lawmakers to postpone the exam until stronger anti-cheating measures are in place, telling a legislative hearing that a delay would cause “even a larger disruption” to students. Choi said that he was confident that proctors could spot AI-powered smart glasses, which typically have thick, horn-rimmed frames. Education authorities are also offering guidance on detecting devices such as microcameras, Education Ministry officials said. Worries about cheating deepened over the weekend after a 34-year-old man who scored the highest on a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a hidden microcamera and smartphone to get answers from AI. Han Won-seok’s unusually high scores had drawn suspicion after he discussed them during recent media interviews. The case follows other incidents involving AI-assisted cheating in the past several months, including test-takers caught using AI-powered smart glasses on an English standardized test in June and on some university essay exams in October. In a video posted Sunday on his lawyer’s YouTube channel, Han said that he used a concealed camera to capture the questions, fed the images to a generative AI tool and received answers on a smartphone. He said that he would cooperate with police, who are investigating the case. Han had previously said that he scored 397.5 out of a possible 400 points on the first-stage, multiple-choice test in April, and 663 out of 800 on the second-stage essay exam in July, unusually high marks that one Korean newspaper likened to “running a 100-meter sprint in under five seconds.” The national college entrance exam, known as “Suneung,” or the College Scholastic Ability Test, is a high-stakes annual event in a country notorious for intense academic competition, where prospects for jobs, social standing and even marriage can depend on which university a person attends. South Korea goes to great lengths each year to create an ideal testing environment, effectively bringing the country to a standstill by delaying the start of the workday and stock market trading to ease traffic for test-takers and pausing flights during the English listening section of the exam. Police officers often use cars and motorcycles to escort test-takers who are running late, while the military sometimes suspends training in areas near testing sites. But it’s difficult for authorities to come up with equally sweeping measures to prevent cheating with AI devices, which the Seoul-based Hankyoreh newspaper warned in an editorial Monday could threaten “the very foundations of the examination system.” Education authorities had focused for months on preventing the use of AI-powered glasses, but Han’s case has raised doubts about whether they are prepared for cheating involving other, less conspicuous devices. Education authorities will deploy at least one specially trained supervisor at each of the 1,300 test sites nationwide to identify such glasses. Officials also are considering requiring test takers to hand over their smart devices and shutting down public Wi-Fi connections at test sites, according to Prime Minister Han Seongsook’s office. Song Geun-hyeon, another senior Education Ministry official, said that the ministry has provided proctors with new guidance on detecting test-takers using hidden cameras and other devices, including watching for suspicious movements involving “their sleeves, collars or buttons, and certain gestures.” The ministry was working with the Ministry of Science and Information and Communication Technology on anti-cheating measures for the college entrance exam, which are due to be announced on Tuesday. Vice Education Minister Choi Eun-ok said that the discussions with the science ministry also include temporarily restricting telecommunications at test sites. It wasn’t immediately clear whether that’s feasible, considering laws prohibiting electronic signal jamming, or concerns that it could interfere with communication in surrounding areas. Song said that metal detectors and radio detectors would be limited, while deploying thermal cameras would be highly unlikely because of privacy concerns. Supervisors can’t search belongings without the consent of the test-takers. “At the government-wide level, we would also need to give further consideration to measures that will make it easier to identify (AI) smart devices,” said Song, adding that officials are debating whether to require manufacturers to design the devices to emit “flashing lights or sounds” while in use. mart glasses, which typically have thick, horn-rimmed frames. Education authorities are also offering guidance on detecting devices such as microcameras, Education Ministry officials said.

articles.title: Flight delays, cancellations return to normal levels after weekend of travel chaos
articles.summary: Air travel across the United States was largely returning to normal Monday, although some disruption persisted as airlines scrambled to get back on schedule after a rare nationwide ground stop.
articles.body: Air travel across the United States was largely returning to normal Monday, although some disruption persisted as airlines scrambled to get back on schedule after a rare nationwide ground stop. The extraordinary shutdown saw thousands of fed up passengers stranded, some sleeping in terminals and missing meetings and family occasions. The fallout from Friday’s stoppage was still being felt, with officials blaming a router issue that derailed air traffic control communications. But by 9 a.m. ET Monday, about 1,500 flights into and out of the U.S. were delayed and nearly 300 canceled, a dramatic drop from the 10,987 delayed and 2,336 canceled U.S. flights Sunday, according to the aviation data site FlightAware. American Airlines had the largest number of canceled flights Monday at 157, followed by SkyWest with 38 flights. Dallas-Fort Worth International and Chicago O’Hare International were the origin airports experiencing the highest number of cancellations Monday, according to data from FlightAware. However, the outlook for the coming days is set to improve with just 3 U.S. flights due to be canceled Tuesday, as passengers gear up for busy Thanksgiving travel later this month. “It takes some time for the airlines to rechoreograph all of their crews and aircraft. We’re going to start seeing things get better today, but I think back to normal tomorrow,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday. The nationwide ground stop lasted several hours Friday and stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers across the country. The Federal Aviation Administration lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday. It was the longest nationwide halt to U.S. air travel since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on the United States. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said authorities had found no evidence of a cyberattack. Duffy on Sunday declined to apologize for the ground stop, instead blaming his predecessors and previous presidential administrations that he said did not do enough to modernize the nation’s air traffic control system. “It happened on my watch, but we have to be clear: I am moving at an incredible speed that no one has done at the FAA or in decades,” Duffy told NBC News’ “Meet the Press.” “But I can’t apologize for what was passed off to us, and I can’t blame Republicans or Democrats because it’s all of them.” FAA contractor L3Harris had been working on replacing a copper line with a fiber line at a remote site in El Dorado, Arkansas. Duffy said Sunday that the replacement triggered problems with another recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas, which started broadcasting and overloading routers at other air traffic control centers across the country. The FAA said it still does not know what ultimately caused the problem that occurred with maintenance work that had been done thousands of times ​before without issue, Duffy added. Copper-to-fiber optic telecommunications conversions are being completed at FAA facilities around the country at a rapid pace. More than 3,500 communication lines have been replaced out of the 5,170 slated to be switched out by 2028, according to FAA data. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the surge overwhelmed routers at one center and then spread to backup routers at other locations. He said the FAA halted departures to relieve pressure on the system while officials worked to identify the source of the problem. “I think that was the right call,” Bedford said. “We stand behind that.” Officials are investigating why the router behaved that way. Friday’s disruption is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a U.S. air traffic control system beset by aging technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers. President Donald Trump on Sunday called for additional funding from lawmakers, while senior Democrats were skeptical of pleas for more money, pointing to unspent funds. Duffy said that the money unspent last year was earmarked only for certain spending, and did not include funds for new software to manage the airspace.

articles.title: French actor Gerard Depardieu withdraws his sexual assault appeal, apologizes to victims
articles.summary: French actor Gérard Depardieu on Monday withdrew his appeal against a 2025 conviction for sexual assault, accepting his guilt and apologizing to his victims.
articles.body: French actor Gérard Depardieu on Monday withdrew his appeal against a 2025 conviction for sexual assault, accepting his guilt and apologizing to his victims. In a statement, Depardieu said he had often used “vulgar, sexually suggestive humor” on set and now realized “there is a line between cheekiness and offence.” He said he offered “his deepest and most sincere apologies to all those who may have suffered as a result,” adding that he had chosen to pull his appeal as he had “come to realize that I belonged to a world that no longer exists.” Depardieu — a towering figure in French cinema, who starred in more than 200 films over five decades, including Green Card, The Last Metro and Cyrano de Bergerac — was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a film set in May 2025. He received an 18-month suspended sentence, with the judge saying he appeared not to have grasped the “traumatic” impact of his behavior. Depardieu still faces the prospect of a trial in the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. He denies guilt.
